verses.text: These are the words Moses spoke to all Israel across the Jordan, in the wilderness of the Arabah opposite Suf, between Paran, Tophel, Laban, Hazeroth, and Dizahab.
It’s an eleven-day walk from Horeb to Kadesh Barnea by way of Mount Seir.
On day one of month eleven in year forty, Moses told the Israelites everything Yahweh had commanded him to tell them.
This was after Moses defeated Sihon, king of the Amorites, who lived in Heshbon, and defeated Og, king of Bashan, who lived in Ashtaroth, at Edrei.
Across the Jordan in Moab, Moses began to explain this law:
“Yahweh our God told us at Horeb, ‘You’ve been at this mountain long enough.

Turn around and get moving. Head for the Amorite hill country and all the places around it: the Arabah, the hills, the lowlands, the South, the coast, the land of the Canaanites, and Lebanon all the way to the great Euphrates River.
Look, I’ve put the land right in front of you. Go in and take the land Yahweh swore to give your ancestors Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob, and their descendants after them.’”
At that time I told you, “I can’t carry all of you by myself.
Yahweh your God has grown your numbers, and now there are as many of you as stars in the sky. ✨
May Yahweh, the God of your ancestors, make you a thousand times more numerous and bless you just as he promised!
How am I supposed to handle all your problems, burdens, and arguments on my own?
Choose wise, understanding, respected men from your tribes, and I’ll put them in charge.”
You answered, “That sounds like the right thing to do.”
So I took wise and respected men from your tribes and put them in charge of you. I appointed commanders over thousands, hundreds, fifties, and tens, and officers for your tribes.
At that time I told your judges, “Hear the cases people bring you and judge fairly between one person and another, including the foreigner living among you.

Don’t play favorites. Listen to the least important person just as you would to the most important. Don’t let anybody intimidate you, because the judgment belongs to God. If a case is too hard for you, bring it to me and I’ll hear it.”
At that time I gave you all the instructions you needed to follow.
We left Horeb and traveled through that huge, frightening wilderness you saw, taking the road to the Amorite hill country as Yahweh our God told us. Then we came to Kadesh Barnea.
I told you, “You’ve reached the Amorite hill country that Yahweh our God is giving us.
Look, Yahweh your God has put the land in front of you. Go up and take it, just as Yahweh, the God of your ancestors, told you. Don’t be afraid or lose heart.”
Every one of you came to me and said, “Let’s send some men ahead to scout the land. They can report back on which road we should take and what towns we’ll come to.”
That seemed like a good idea to me, so I selected twelve men, one from each tribe.
They went up into the hill country, reached the valley of Eshcol, and scouted it.
They brought back some fruit from the land and gave us this report: “The land Yahweh our God is giving us is good.”
But you refused to go up. You went against what Yahweh your God told you to do.
You grumbled in your tents, saying, “Yahweh must hate us. He brought us out of Egypt just to hand us over to the Amorites and have them wipe us out.

Where are we supposed to go? Our brothers have scared us out of our minds. They said, ‘The people are bigger and taller than us. Their cities are huge, with walls that reach the sky. We even saw descendants of the Anakim there!’”
Then I told you, “Don’t panic. Don’t be afraid of them.
Yahweh your God goes ahead of you. He’ll fight for you just as he did in Egypt, right in front of your eyes,
and in the wilderness. You saw how Yahweh your God carried you like a father carries his son, every step of the way until you got here.”
Even after all that, you didn’t trust Yahweh your God.
He went ahead of you on the road to find places for you to put up your tents. He showed you which way to go with fire at night and a cloud by day.
Yahweh heard what you said. He got angry and swore:
“None of the men of this wicked generation will see the good land I promised your ancestors,
except Caleb son of Jephunneh. He’ll see it. I’ll give the land he walked on to him and his children, because he followed Yahweh wholeheartedly.”
Yahweh was angry with me because of you too. He told me, “You won’t go in either.
Joshua son of Nun, who stands before you, will go in. Encourage him, because he’ll lead Israel into its inheritance.
The little ones you said would be captured or killed, your children who don’t yet know good from evil, will go in. I’ll give them the land, and they’ll take possession of it.
As for you, turn around and head into the wilderness by the road to the Red Sea.”
Then you told me, “We’ve sinned against Yahweh. We’ll go up and fight, just as Yahweh our God told us to.” Every one of you strapped on your weapons and figured you could just head up into the hills.
Yahweh told me, “Tell them, ‘Don’t go up or fight. I’m not with you, and your enemies will strike you down.’”
I told you, but you wouldn’t listen. You went against Yahweh’s command and marched up into the hills anyway.
The Amorites who lived in those hills came out against you. They chased you like bees and beat you back through Seir as far as Hormah.
You came back and cried before Yahweh, but he wouldn’t listen to you or turn his ear toward you.
So you stayed in Kadesh for a long time, all those days you spent there.
Then we turned and headed into the wilderness by the road to the Red Sea, just as Yahweh told me. We traveled around Mount Seir for many days.
Yahweh spoke to me:
“You’ve been going around this mountain long enough. Turn north.
Tell the people, ‘You’re about to pass through territory that belongs to your relatives, Esau’s descendants who live in Seir. They’ll be afraid of you, so be careful.
Don’t pick a fight with them. I won’t give you any of their land, even enough to put one foot on. I gave Mount Seir to Esau as his own land.
Pay them for the food you eat and the water you drink.’”

Yahweh your God has blessed everything you’ve worked at. He’s watched over your journey through this vast wilderness. For forty years Yahweh your God has been with you, and you haven’t gone without a thing.
So we went past our relatives, Esau’s descendants who live in Seir. We left the Arabah road from Elath and Ezion Geber and turned onto the road through Moab’s wilderness.
Yahweh told me, “Don’t harass the Moabites or pick a fight with them. I won’t give you any of their land to own. I’ve given Ar to Lot’s descendants as their own land.”
(The Emim used to live there. They were a great people, numerous and as tall as the Anakim.
Like the Anakim, they were counted among the Rephaim. The Moabites called them Emim.
The Horites used to live in Seir too, but Esau’s descendants drove them out, destroyed them, and settled in their place. Israel did the same in the land Yahweh gave them to own.)
“Now get up and cross the Zered Brook.” So we crossed the Zered Brook.
Thirty-eight years passed between leaving Kadesh Barnea and crossing the Zered Brook. By then the whole generation of fighting men had died out in the camp, just as Yahweh had sworn to them.
Yahweh’s hand was against them until they’d all been removed from the camp.
Once all those fighting men had died out among the people,
Yahweh spoke to me:
“Today you’ll pass through Ar, on the border of Moab.
When you get near the Ammonites’ border, don’t harass them or start a fight. I won’t give you any of their land. I gave it to Lot’s descendants as their own land.”
(That too was considered Rephaim territory. The Rephaim lived there before, but the Ammonites called them Zamzummim.
They were a great people, numerous and as tall as the Anakim. But Yahweh destroyed them ahead of Israel, and the Ammonites took their place and settled there.
He’d done the same for Esau’s descendants who live in Seir. He destroyed the Horites ahead of them, and they took their place and have lived there to this day.
The Avvim used to live in villages as far as Gaza. The Caphtorim came from Caphtor, destroyed them, and settled in their place.)
“Get up, set out, and cross the Arnon Valley. Look, I’ve handed you Sihon the Amorite, king of Heshbon, and his land. Start taking possession of it and engage him in battle.
Starting today I’ll make peoples everywhere under the sky dread you. When they hear about you, they’ll shake with fear and be in anguish because of you.”
From the wilderness of Kedemoth I sent messengers to Sihon, king of Heshbon, with a peaceful message:
“Let me cross your land. I’ll stay on the highway the whole way, without turning to the right or left.
Sell me food to eat and water to drink. I’ll pay for both. Just let me walk through,
as Esau’s descendants in Seir and the Moabites in Ar let me do, until I cross the Jordan into the land Yahweh our God is giving us.”
But Sihon, king of Heshbon, refused to let us cross. Yahweh your God made his spirit stubborn and his heart set against us so he could hand him over to you, as he’s done today.
Yahweh told me, “Look, I’ve started handing over Sihon and his land to you. Go ahead and take possession of it as your inheritance.”
Then Sihon and all his people came out to fight us at Jahaz.
Yahweh our God handed him over to us, and we struck him down along with his sons and all his people.
We took all his towns and destroyed every inhabited town completely, killing the women and the little ones too. We left no survivors.
We took only the livestock and the goods from the towns we captured as plunder for ourselves.
From Aroer on the edge of the Arnon Valley and the town down in the valley all the way to Gilead, no town was too high for us. Yahweh our God handed them all over to us.
But you stayed away from Ammonite territory, including the banks of the Jabbok River, the towns in the hill country, and everywhere else Yahweh our God had told us to stay away from.
Then we turned and headed up the road to Bashan. Og, the king of Bashan, came out with all his people to fight us at Edrei.
Yahweh told me, “Don’t be afraid of him. I’ve handed him over to you, along with all his people and his land. Do to him what you did to Sihon, the Amorite king who lived in Heshbon.”
So Yahweh our God handed Og, the king of Bashan, and all his people over to us too. We struck them down and left no survivors.
At that time we took all his towns. We didn’t leave a single one untaken: sixty towns, the whole region of Argob in Og’s kingdom in Bashan.
Those towns were all fortified with high walls, gates, and bars. There were also a great many villages without walls.
We destroyed them completely, just as we did to Sihon, king of Heshbon. We destroyed every inhabited town, including the women and the little ones.
We kept all the livestock and everything we took from the towns as plunder for ourselves.
At that time we took the land from the two Amorite kings across the Jordan, from the Arnon Valley all the way to Mount Hermon.
(The Sidonians call Hermon Sirion, while the Amorites call it Senir.)
We took all the towns on the plain, all of Gilead, and all of Bashan as far as Salecah and Edrei, towns in Og’s kingdom in Bashan.
(Og, king of Bashan, was the last one left of the Rephaim. His bed was made of iron. Isn’t it still in Rabbah of the Ammonites? It was nine cubits long and four cubits wide, by the standard cubit.)
Here’s how I divided the land we took then. I gave the Reubenites and Gadites the land from Aroer by the Arnon Valley, plus half the hill country of Gilead and its towns.
I gave the rest of Gilead and all of Bashan, Og’s kingdom, to the half-tribe of Manasseh. That included the whole region of Argob, all of Bashan. (It’s also known as the land of the Rephaim.
Jair son of Manasseh took the whole region of Argob, right up to the border of the Geshurites and Maacathites. He named those places in Bashan after himself, and they’re still called Havvoth Jair.)
I gave Gilead to Machir.
I gave the Reubenites and Gadites the land from Gilead to the Arnon Valley, with the middle of the valley as the border, and out to the Jabbok River, the border of the Ammonites.
I also gave them the Arabah, with the Jordan as its border from Chinnereth to the Sea of the Arabah, the Salt Sea, below the eastern slopes of Pisgah.
At that time I told you, “Yahweh your God has given you this land as your own. All your fighting men will cross over armed ahead of your fellow Israelites.
Your wives, children, and livestock will stay in the towns I gave you. I know you’ve got a lot of livestock.

Stay with your brothers until Yahweh gives them rest as he gave you rest, and they take possession of the land Yahweh your God is giving them across the Jordan. Then each of you can go back to the land I gave you.”
At that time I told Joshua, “You saw with your own eyes what Yahweh your God did to these two kings. Yahweh will do the same to all the kingdoms you’re going to cross into.
Don’t be afraid of them. Yahweh your God himself fights for you.”
At that time I pleaded with God:
“Lord Yahweh, you’ve started to show your servant how great you are and how strong your hand is. What god in heaven or on earth can do the mighty things you do?
Please let me cross over and see the good land beyond the Jordan, that beautiful mountain and Lebanon.”
But Yahweh was angry with me because of you and wouldn’t listen. He told me, “Enough! Don’t bring this up with me again.
Go up to the top of Pisgah. Look west, north, south, and east, and see it for yourself. You won’t cross this Jordan.
Give Joshua his charge, encourage him, and make him strong. He’ll cross ahead of these people and lead them into the land you’re about to see, so it becomes their inheritance.”
So we stayed in the valley near Beth Peor.
Israel, listen to the laws and rulings I’m teaching you, and put them into practice. Then you’ll live and go in and take possession of the land Yahweh, the God of your ancestors, is giving you.
Don’t add to what I command or take anything away. Keep the commands of Yahweh your God that I’m giving you.
You saw with your own eyes what Yahweh did at Baal Peor. Yahweh your God wiped out everyone among you who followed Baal of Peor.
But all of you who held on to Yahweh your God are alive today.
Look, I’ve taught you laws and rulings just as Yahweh my God commanded me, so you’ll live by them in the land you’re going to take as your own.
Keep them and do them. That’s how other peoples will see your wisdom and understanding. When they hear these laws, they’ll say, “This great nation really is a wise and understanding people.”
What other great nation has a god as close as Yahweh our God is whenever we call on him?
What other great nation has laws and rulings as fair as this whole law I’m giving you today?
So watch yourselves closely. Don’t forget what you saw with your own eyes or let it slip out of your heart as long as you live. Tell your children and grandchildren about it,

about the day you stood before Yahweh your God at Horeb. Yahweh told me, “Gather the people to me so I can let them hear my words. Then they’ll learn to show me reverence as long as they live on earth, and they’ll teach their children.”
You came up and stood at the foot of the mountain. It burned right up to the heart of the sky, with clouds and deep darkness. 🔥
Yahweh spoke to you from the middle of the fire. You heard the words, but you didn’t see any shape. All you heard was a voice.
He told you his covenant and commanded you to keep it. Those were the Ten Commandments, and he wrote them on two stone tablets.
At that time Yahweh told me to teach you the laws and rulings so you could live by them in the land you’re crossing over to possess.
Watch yourselves closely. You didn’t see any shape the day Yahweh spoke to you at Horeb from the middle of the fire.
Don’t corrupt yourselves by carving an image in any shape, whether it looks like a man or a woman,
an animal that lives on earth, a winged bird that flies in the sky,
anything that crawls on the ground, or any fish in the waters below the earth.

When you look up and see the sun, moon, stars, and the whole host of heaven, don’t let them pull you into bowing down to them and serving them. Yahweh your God has allotted them to all peoples under the sky.
But Yahweh took you and brought you out of Egypt, that iron furnace, to be his own people, just as you are today.
Yahweh was angry with me because of you. He swore I wouldn’t cross the Jordan or enter that good land Yahweh your God is giving you to inherit.
I’ll die in this land. I won’t cross the Jordan. You’ll cross and take possession of that good land.
Be careful that you don’t forget the covenant Yahweh your God made with you and carve an image in any shape he’s forbidden.
Yahweh your God is a fire that consumes, a jealous God.

After you’ve had children and grandchildren and lived in the land a long time, if you corrupt yourselves by carving an image in any shape and do what’s evil in Yahweh your God’s sight, provoking his anger,
I call heaven and earth to witness against you today: you’ll quickly perish from the land you’re crossing the Jordan to possess. You won’t last long there. You’ll be completely destroyed.
Yahweh will scatter you among other peoples. Only a few of you will be left among the nations where he sends you.
There you’ll serve gods made by human hands out of wood and stone. They can’t see, hear, eat, or smell.
But from there you’ll look for Yahweh your God. If you seek him with your whole heart and your whole being, you’ll find him.
When you’re in distress and all these things have happened to you, in days to come you’ll return to Yahweh your God and listen to him.
Yahweh your God is merciful. He won’t abandon you, destroy you, or forget the covenant he swore to your ancestors.

Ask about the past, going all the way back to the day God created human beings on earth. From one end of the sky to the other, has anything this great ever happened? Has anyone even heard of anything like it?
Has a people ever heard God speak from the middle of fire, the way you did, and lived to tell about it?

Has any god ever gone and taken a nation for himself out of another nation with trials, signs, wonders, war, a mighty hand, an outstretched arm, and terrifying acts, the way Yahweh your God did for you in Egypt right before your eyes?
You saw it so you’d know that Yahweh is God. There’s nobody else besides him.
He let you hear his voice from heaven to teach you. On earth he showed you his great fire, and you heard his words from the middle of it.
Because he loved your ancestors, he chose their descendants after them. He brought you out of Egypt in his own presence and by his great power
to drive out nations bigger and stronger than you, bring you into their land, and give it to you as your inheritance, just as he’s doing today.
So know this today and take it to heart: Yahweh himself is God in heaven above and on earth below. There’s nobody else.
Keep his laws and the commands I’m giving you today so things will go well for you and your children after you, and you’ll live long in the land Yahweh your God is giving you for all time.
Then Moses set apart three towns east of the Jordan, toward the sunrise.
Anyone who killed a neighbor by accident and hadn’t hated that person before could run to one of those towns and live.
They were Bezer in the wilderness on the plain for the Reubenites, Ramoth in Gilead for the Gadites, and Golan in Bashan for the Manassites.
This is the law Moses set before the Israelites.
These are the testimonies, laws, and rulings Moses gave the Israelites when they came out of Egypt.
He gave them across the Jordan, in the valley opposite Beth Peor, in the land of Sihon, the Amorite king who lived in Heshbon. Moses and the Israelites defeated him after they came out of Egypt.
They took possession of his land and the land of Og, king of Bashan. Those were the two Amorite kings east of the Jordan, toward the sunrise.
Their territory went from Aroer, on the edge of the Arnon Valley, to Mount Siyon, also called Hermon.
It also included the whole Arabah east of the Jordan, all the way to the Sea of the Arabah below the slopes of Pisgah.
Moses called all Israel together and said, “Israel, listen to the laws and rulings I’m giving you today. Learn them and make sure you live by them.”
Yahweh our God made a covenant with us at Horeb.
Yahweh made this covenant with us, every one of us alive here today, and not with our ancestors.
Yahweh spoke with you face to face on the mountain, right from the middle of the fire.
I stood between Yahweh and you that day to tell you what he said, because the fire scared you and you didn’t go up the mountain. He said:
“I’m Yahweh your God. I brought you out of Egypt, out of the place where you were slaves.
“Have no other gods before me.
“Don’t carve an image for yourself in the shape of anything in heaven above, on the earth below, or in the waters under the earth.

Don’t bow down to those images or serve them. I, Yahweh your God, am a jealous God. I bring the consequences of the parents’ wrongdoing on their children, to the third and fourth generation of those who hate me.
But I show faithful love to thousands who love me and keep my commands.
“Don’t misuse the name of Yahweh your God. Yahweh won’t let anyone who misuses his name go guilt-free.
“Keep the Sabbath day holy, just as Yahweh your God told you.
Work for six days and do everything you need to do.

The seventh day is a Sabbath for Yahweh your God. Nobody does any work that day: you, your son, your daughter, your male or female servant, your ox, your donkey, any of your livestock, or the foreigner living in your town. Your servants should get to rest just like you do.
Remember that you were a slave in Egypt. Yahweh your God brought you out with a mighty hand and an outstretched arm. That’s why Yahweh your God told you to keep the Sabbath.
“Honor your father and mother, just as Yahweh your God told you, so you’ll live long and things will go well for you in the land Yahweh your God is giving you.
“Don’t murder.
“Don’t commit adultery.
“Don’t steal.
“Don’t give false testimony against your neighbor.
“Don’t covet your neighbor’s wife. Don’t set your sights on your neighbor’s house, field, male or female servant, ox, donkey, or anything else they own.”

Yahweh spoke those words in a loud voice to your whole assembly on the mountain, from the fire, the cloud, and the thick darkness. He added nothing more. He wrote the words on two stone tablets and handed them to me.
When you heard the voice from the middle of the darkness while the mountain burned with fire, your tribal leaders and elders all came over to me.
You said, “Yahweh our God has shown us his glory and greatness. We heard his voice right out of the fire. Today we’ve seen that God can speak to a person and that person can live.
So why should we die now? This huge fire will swallow us up. If we hear Yahweh our God speak again, we’ll die.
Who else has heard the living God speaking from the middle of a fire the way we did and lived?
You go closer and listen to everything Yahweh our God says. Then tell us everything he tells you. We’ll listen and do it.”
Yahweh heard what you said to me. He told me, “I heard what these people said to you. They were right in everything they said.
If only their hearts would stay like this, so they’d honor me with reverence and keep all my commands always. Then things would go well for them and their children forever!
“Go tell them to head back to their tents.
You stay here with me. I’ll give you all the commands, laws, and rulings you’re to teach them, so they can live by them in the land I’m giving them to own.”
So be careful to do what Yahweh your God commanded you. Don’t turn off to the right or the left.
Follow the whole path Yahweh your God laid out for you. Then you’ll live, things will go well for you, and you’ll spend many years in the land you’re going to possess.
Here are the commands, laws, and rulings Yahweh your God told me to teach you. Live by them in the land you’re crossing over to possess.
Honor Yahweh your God with reverence. Keep all the laws and commands I’m giving you, you, your children, and your grandchildren, for as long as you live, so your lives will be long.

Listen, Israel, and make sure you do what he says. Then things will go well for you, and your numbers will grow across a land flowing with milk and honey, just as Yahweh, the God of your ancestors, promised you.
Listen, Israel: Yahweh is our God. Yahweh is one.
Love Yahweh your God with your whole heart, your whole soul, and all your strength.
Keep these words I’m giving you today close to your heart.
Teach them carefully to your children. Talk about them when you sit at home, when you walk along the road, when you lie down, and when you get up.
Tie them to your hand as a sign and wear them as a reminder between your eyes.
Write them on your doorposts and on your gates.
Yahweh your God will bring you into the land he swore to give your ancestors Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob. It has great, good towns you didn’t build,
houses full of good things you didn’t put there, water tanks you didn’t dig, and vineyards and olive trees you didn’t plant. When you eat until you’re full,
watch out that you don’t forget Yahweh, who brought you out of Egypt, out of the place where you were slaves.
Honor Yahweh your God with reverence. Serve him and swear your oaths in his name.
Don’t go chasing other gods, the gods of the peoples around you.
Yahweh your God is right here among you, and he’s a jealous God. Don’t stir up his anger against you or he’ll wipe you off the face of the earth.
Don’t put Yahweh your God to the test like you did at Massah.
Be careful to keep every command, testimony, and law Yahweh your God has given you.
Do what’s right and good in Yahweh’s eyes. Then things will go well for you, and you’ll go in and take possession of the good land he promised your ancestors.
He’ll drive all your enemies out ahead of you, just as he said.
One day your child will ask, “What do the testimonies, laws, and rulings Yahweh our God gave you mean?”
Tell your child, “We were Pharaoh’s slaves in Egypt, and Yahweh brought us out of Egypt with a mighty hand.
Right before our eyes, Yahweh brought great and terrifying signs and wonders against Egypt, Pharaoh, and his whole household.
He brought us out of there so he could bring us here and give us the land he promised our ancestors.
Yahweh told us to live by all these laws and honor Yahweh our God with reverence. He gave them for our lasting good, to keep us alive as we are today.
It’ll count as righteousness for us if we’re careful to follow all these commands before Yahweh our God, just as he told us.”

When Yahweh your God brings you into the land you’re going to possess, he’ll drive out many nations ahead of you: the Hittites, Girgashites, Amorites, Canaanites, Perizzites, Hivites, and Jebusites. These are seven nations bigger and stronger than you.
When Yahweh your God hands them over and you defeat them, destroy them completely. Make no treaty with them and show them no mercy.
Don’t marry into their families. Don’t give your daughter to one of their sons or take one of their daughters for your son.
They’d turn your sons away from following me, and your sons would serve other gods. Yahweh’s anger would flare against you, and he’d destroy you quickly.
Here’s how you’re to deal with their worship sites: tear down their altars, smash their sacred pillars, cut down their Asherah poles, and burn their carved images.
You’re a people set apart as holy to Yahweh your God. Out of all the peoples on earth, Yahweh your God chose you to be his own.
Yahweh didn’t set his love on you or choose you because you outnumbered anyone. You were the smallest of all peoples.
He loved you and wanted to keep the oath he swore to your ancestors. That’s why Yahweh brought you out with a mighty hand and rescued you from slavery, from the grip of Pharaoh, king of Egypt.
Know who Yahweh your God is. He himself is God, the faithful God who keeps his covenant and shows faithful love for a thousand generations to those who love him and keep his commands.
He pays back those who hate him right to their faces, destroying them. He won’t hold back or delay. He’ll repay them to their faces.
So keep the commands, laws, and rulings I’m giving you today and put them into practice.
If you listen to these rulings and live by them, Yahweh your God will keep his covenant with you and show you the faithful love he swore to your ancestors.

He’ll love you, bless you, and grow your numbers. In the land he promised your ancestors, he’ll bless your children and your harvests, your grain, new wine, and oil, the calves in your herds and the young in your flocks.
You’ll be blessed more than all other peoples. None of your men or women will be unable to have children, and none of your livestock will be barren.
Yahweh will keep all sickness away from you. None of those terrible diseases you knew in Egypt will fall on you. He’ll put them on those who hate you.
You’ll wipe out all the peoples Yahweh your God hands over to you. Don’t look on them with pity or serve their gods. That would be a trap for you.
You might think, “These nations outnumber me. How am I going to drive them out?”
Don’t be afraid of them. Remember what Yahweh your God did to Pharaoh and all Egypt.

You saw the great trials, signs, and wonders with your own eyes. You saw the mighty hand and outstretched arm that Yahweh your God used to bring you out. He’ll do the same to the peoples you’re afraid of.
Yahweh your God will send the hornet among them too, until even those who survive and go into hiding perish before you.
Don’t be scared of them. Yahweh your God is right here among you, a great and awesome God.
Yahweh your God will drive those nations out ahead of you little by little. You can’t wipe them out all at once, or the wild animals will multiply around you.
Yahweh your God will hand them over to you and throw them into such confusion that they’ll be destroyed.
He’ll hand over their kings, and you’ll wipe out their names from under the sky. Nobody will be able to stand against you until you’ve destroyed them.
Burn the carved images of their gods. Don’t go after the silver or gold on them or take it for yourself. It could trap you, because Yahweh your God finds it detestable.
Don’t bring anything detestable into your house, or you’ll be marked for destruction just like it. Despise it completely and treat it with disgust, because it’s marked for destruction.
Be careful to do everything I’m commanding you today. Then you’ll live, grow in number, and go in and take possession of the land Yahweh promised your ancestors.
Remember the whole road Yahweh your God led you down for forty years in the wilderness. He humbled you and tested you to see what was in your heart and whether you’d keep his commands.

He humbled you, let you go hungry, and fed you manna, food that neither you nor your ancestors had ever known. He was teaching you that people need more than bread to live. They live by every word that comes from Yahweh’s mouth.
For all forty of those years, your clothes didn’t wear out and your feet didn’t swell.
Take this to heart: Yahweh your God disciplines you the way a father disciplines his son.
Keep Yahweh your God’s commands, live the way he tells you, and honor him with reverence.
Yahweh your God is bringing you into a good land, with streams, springs, and underground waters flowing into hills and valleys.
It’s a land of wheat and barley, grapevines, fig trees, and pomegranates, a land of olive trees and honey.
You’ll have all the bread you need there and won’t go without anything. Its rocks are iron, and you can dig copper out of its hills.
When you’ve eaten your fill, bless Yahweh your God for the good land he’s given you.
Watch out that you don’t forget Yahweh your God by failing to keep the commands, rulings, and laws I’m giving you today.
You’ll eat your fill, build fine homes, and move into them.
Your herds and flocks will grow, your silver and gold will pile up, and everything you own will increase.
When that happens, don’t let pride go to your head and make you forget Yahweh your God, who brought you out of Egypt, out of slavery.
He led you through that huge, terrifying wilderness, with venomous snakes, scorpions, and dry ground with no water. He poured water for you out of hard flint.
He fed you manna in the wilderness, food your ancestors had never known. He did it to humble you, test you, and do you good in the end.
Don’t start thinking, “I got all this wealth by my own power and the strength of my own hands.”
Remember Yahweh your God. He’s the one who gives you the power to gain wealth, so he can establish the covenant he swore to your ancestors, as he’s doing today.
If you forget Yahweh your God, chase after other gods, serve them, and bow down to them, I warn you today that you’ll perish.
You’ll perish just like the nations Yahweh destroys ahead of you, because you refused to listen to Yahweh your God.
Listen, Israel! Today you’re crossing the Jordan to take land from nations bigger and stronger than you. Their cities are huge, with walls that reach the sky.
The people are big and tall. They’re descendants of the Anakim. You know who they are and have heard people say, “Who can stand up to the sons of Anak?”

Know this today: Yahweh your God is crossing ahead of you like a fire that devours everything. He’ll destroy them and bring them down before you. You’ll drive them out and wipe them out quickly, just as Yahweh told you.
After Yahweh your God drives them out ahead of you, don’t think, “Yahweh brought me into this land because I’m righteous.” It’s because of these nations’ wickedness that he’s driving them out.

You’re not getting their land because you’re righteous or your heart is upright. Yahweh your God is driving out these nations because of their wickedness and to keep the promise he swore to your ancestors Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob.
Understand this: Yahweh your God isn’t giving you this good land because you’re righteous. You’re a stubborn people.
Remember how you made Yahweh your God angry in the wilderness, and don’t ever forget it. From the day you left Egypt until you got here, you’ve been rebelling against him.
You made Yahweh so angry at Horeb that he was ready to destroy you.
When I went up the mountain for the stone tablets, the tablets of the covenant Yahweh made with you, I stayed there forty days and forty nights. I ate no bread and drank no water.
Yahweh handed me the two stone tablets with writing from God’s own finger. They held every word Yahweh spoke to you from the middle of the fire on the mountain the day you all gathered.
At the end of forty days and forty nights, Yahweh gave me those two stone tablets, the tablets of the covenant.

Yahweh told me, “Get up and get down from here fast. The people you brought out of Egypt have corrupted themselves. They turned away from what I told them to do so quickly. They’ve cast a metal idol for themselves!”
Yahweh went on, “I’ve watched these people, and look how stubborn they are.
Leave me alone so I can destroy them and wipe their name from under the sky. I’ll make you into a bigger and stronger nation than they are.”
So I turned and went down the mountain while it was burning with fire. I carried the two covenant tablets in my hands.
I looked, and there it was: you’d sinned against Yahweh your God. You’d made yourselves a metal calf. You turned away so quickly from the way Yahweh told you to go.
I grabbed both tablets, threw them down, and smashed them right before your eyes.
I fell facedown before Yahweh again for forty days and forty nights. I ate no bread and drank no water because of all your sin. You did what was evil in Yahweh’s sight and stirred up his anger.
I was afraid of how furious Yahweh was with you. He was ready to destroy you, but he listened to me that time too.
Yahweh was also angry enough with Aaron to destroy him, so I prayed for Aaron at the same time.
I took that calf you’d made, the thing you’d sinned with, and burned it. I crushed it and ground it down to fine dust, then threw the dust into the stream that ran down the mountain.
At Taberah, Massah, and Kibroth Hattaavah, you made Yahweh angry again.
When Yahweh sent you from Kadesh Barnea and said, “Go up and take possession of the land I’ve given you,” you rebelled against Yahweh your God. You didn’t trust him or listen to what he said.
You’ve been rebelling against Yahweh since the day I met you.
So I stayed facedown before Yahweh those forty days and forty nights because he’d said he would destroy you.
I prayed to Yahweh, “Lord Yahweh, don’t destroy your people, your own inheritance. You rescued them by your greatness and brought them out of Egypt with a mighty hand.
Remember your servants Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob. Look past these people’s stubbornness, wickedness, and sin.
Otherwise the people in the land you brought us out of will say, ‘Yahweh couldn’t bring them into the land he promised them. He hated them, so he took them out to kill them in the wilderness.’
They’re still your people and your inheritance. You brought them out with your great power and your outstretched arm.”
At that time Yahweh told me, “Cut two stone tablets like the first ones. Come up to me on the mountain, and make a wooden ark.
I’ll write on these tablets the words that were on the first ones you broke. Then put them in the ark.”
So I made an ark of acacia wood, cut two stone tablets like the first ones, and went up the mountain with the tablets in my hands.
He wrote the same words on them as before, the Ten Commandments Yahweh had spoken to you on the mountain from the middle of the fire the day you gathered. Then Yahweh handed them to me.
I turned and came down the mountain and put the tablets in the ark I’d made. They’re still there, just as Yahweh told me.
(The Israelites traveled from Beeroth Bene Jaakan to Moserah. Aaron died there and was buried there. His son Eleazar took his place as priest.
From there they traveled to Gudgodah, and from Gudgodah to Jotbathah, a land full of streams.
At that time Yahweh set Levi’s tribe apart to carry the ark of his covenant, stand before him and serve him, and bless people in his name. They still do that today.
That’s why Levi has no share of the land or inheritance with his brothers. Yahweh is his inheritance, just as Yahweh your God told him.)
I stayed on the mountain forty days and forty nights, just like the first time. Yahweh listened to me again and chose to spare you.
Yahweh told me, “Get up and lead the people on their journey. They’ll go in and take possession of the land I swore to give their ancestors.”
So, Israel, what does Yahweh your God ask of you? Honor him with reverence, walk in all his ways, love him, and serve him with your whole heart and your whole soul.
Keep Yahweh’s commands and laws that I’m giving you today for your own good.
Look, heaven, the highest heavens, the earth, and everything in it all belong to Yahweh your God.
Yet Yahweh took delight in your ancestors and loved them. He chose their descendants after them, you, out of all peoples, just as it is today.
So circumcise your hearts and stop being so stubborn.
Yahweh your God is God of gods and Lord of lords, the great, mighty, awesome God. He plays no favorites and takes no bribes.
He sees that children without fathers and widows get justice. He loves foreigners and gives them food and clothes.
So love foreigners, because you once lived as foreigners in Egypt.
Honor Yahweh your God with reverence. Serve him, hold on to him, and swear your oaths in his name.
He’s the one you praise. He’s your God, the one who did those great and awesome things for you that you saw with your own eyes.
Your ancestors went down to Egypt with seventy people. Now Yahweh your God has made you as numerous as the stars in the sky. ✨
So love Yahweh your God. Always keep his instructions, laws, rulings, and commands.
Remember this today. I’m speaking to you because your children didn’t experience or see Yahweh your God’s discipline, his greatness, his mighty hand, or his outstretched arm.
They didn’t see the signs and deeds he did in Egypt against Pharaoh, the king of Egypt, and his whole land.

They didn’t see what he did to Egypt’s army, its horses, and its chariots. He swept the waters of the Red Sea over them as they were chasing you. To this day, they’re gone because Yahweh destroyed them.
They didn’t see what he did for you in the wilderness until you came here.

They didn’t see what he did to Dathan and Abiram, the sons of Eliab son of Reuben. Right in the middle of Israel, the earth opened its mouth and swallowed them and their households, their tents, and every living thing following them.
But you saw with your own eyes every great thing Yahweh did.
So keep every command I’m giving you today. Then you’ll be strong enough to cross over and take possession of the land you’re heading into.
You’ll live long in the land Yahweh promised your ancestors and their descendants, a land flowing with milk and honey.
The land you’re about to take over is different from Egypt, where you came from. There you planted seed and watered it by foot like a vegetable garden.
The land you’re crossing into has hills and valleys that drink up rain straight from the sky.
Yahweh your God cares for that land. His eyes are on it all year, from the first day to the last.
If you listen closely to the commands I’m giving you today and love Yahweh your God and serve him with your whole heart and soul,
then I’ll send rain on your land at the proper time, both early and late rains. You’ll bring in your grain, new wine, and oil.
I’ll grow grass in your fields for your livestock, and you’ll eat your fill.
Watch out that your heart isn’t fooled into turning away to serve other gods and bow down to them.
If you do that, Yahweh’s anger will flare against you. He’ll shut the sky so it won’t rain and the land won’t grow crops. You’ll quickly perish from the good land he’s giving you.
Keep these words of mine in your heart and soul. Tie them as a sign on your hand and wear them between your eyes.
Teach them to your children. Talk about them when you sit at home, when you walk along the road, when you lie down, and when you get up.
Write them on the doorposts of your house and on your gates.
Then you and your children will live many days in the land Yahweh promised your ancestors, as long as the heavens are over the earth.
If you take care to follow all the commands I’m giving you, loving Yahweh your God, walking in all his ways, and holding tight to him,
Yahweh will drive all these nations out ahead of you, and you’ll take land from nations bigger and stronger than you.
Every place you set foot will be yours. Your borders will run from the wilderness to Lebanon, and from the Euphrates River to the western sea.
Nobody will be able to stand against you. Yahweh your God will make people afraid of you throughout the land you tread on, just as he told you.
Look, today I’m putting a blessing and a curse in front of you.
The blessing is yours if you listen to the commands of Yahweh your God that I’m giving you today.
The curse comes if you refuse to listen to Yahweh your God’s commands and turn away from the path I’m giving you today to chase after gods you’ve never known.
When Yahweh your God brings you into the land you’re going to own, put the blessing on Mount Gerizim and the curse on Mount Ebal.
Aren’t those mountains across the Jordan, beyond the road toward the sunset, in the land of the Canaanites who live in the Arabah near Gilgal, next to the oaks of Moreh?
You’re going to cross the Jordan to take the land Yahweh your God is giving you. You’ll take possession of it and live there.
Be careful to put into practice all the laws and rulings I’m setting before you today.
Here are the laws and rulings you must carefully follow in the land Yahweh, the God of your ancestors, has given you to own. Keep them as long as you live on earth.
Destroy every place where the nations you’re taking the land from served their gods, on the high mountains, on the hills, and under every green tree.
Tear down their altars, smash their sacred pillars, and burn their Asherah poles. Cut down the carved images of their gods and wipe their names out of those places.
Don’t worship Yahweh your God that way.
Go to the place Yahweh your God chooses from among your tribes to put his name. Seek him where he makes his home and go there.
Bring your burnt offerings, sacrifices, tithes, wave offerings, offerings you’ve vowed to give, offerings you give freely, and the firstborn of your herds and flocks.
Eat there before Yahweh your God. You and your households will celebrate everything you’ve worked at that Yahweh your God has blessed.
Don’t keep doing what we’re doing here today, with everyone deciding for themselves what’s right.
You haven’t yet reached the place of rest or the inheritance Yahweh your God is giving you.
But when you cross the Jordan and settle in the land Yahweh your God gives you as your inheritance, he’ll give you rest from all the enemies around you, and you’ll live in safety.

Then bring everything I tell you to the place Yahweh your God chooses for his name to dwell: your burnt offerings, sacrifices, tithes, wave offerings, and all the choice offerings you’ve vowed to give Yahweh.
Celebrate before Yahweh your God with your sons and daughters, your male and female servants, and the Levite in your town, because the Levite has no share or inheritance with you.
Be careful where you offer your burnt offerings. You can’t just bring them to any place you see.
Bring your burnt offerings to the place Yahweh chooses in one of your tribes. Do everything I’m commanding you there.

You can still slaughter animals and eat meat in any of your towns whenever you want, according to what Yahweh your God has given you. Both clean and unclean people can eat it, just as they can eat gazelle or deer.
Just don’t eat the blood. Pour it onto the ground like water.

You can’t eat these things in your own towns: the tithe of your grain, new wine, or oil, the firstborn of your herds or flocks, any offering you’ve vowed to give, anything you’re giving freely, or your wave offerings.

Eat them in front of Yahweh your God at the place he chooses. Bring your sons and daughters, your male and female servants, and the Levite in your town. Celebrate everything you’ve worked at before Yahweh your God.
Be careful to look after the Levites for as long as you live in your land.
When Yahweh your God expands your territory as he promised, and you say, “I feel like eating meat,” go ahead and eat as much meat as you want.
If the place Yahweh your God chooses for his name is too far away, slaughter animals from the herd or flock Yahweh has given you, as I’ve told you. Eat as much as you like in your own towns.
Eat it the way you’d eat gazelle or deer. Clean and unclean people can eat it alike.
Just make sure you don’t eat the blood, because the blood is the life. Don’t eat the life along with the meat.
Pour the blood onto the ground like water. Don’t eat it.
Keep from eating it so things will go well for you and your children after you. Do what’s right in Yahweh’s eyes.
Take the holy things you’ve set apart and the offerings you’ve vowed to give to the place Yahweh chooses.
Offer both the meat and the blood of your burnt offerings on Yahweh your God’s altar. For your other sacrifices, pour the blood on his altar and eat the meat.
Listen and carefully follow everything I’m telling you. Then things will go well for you and your children forever as you do what’s good and right in Yahweh your God’s eyes.
Yahweh your God will cut off the nations ahead of you when you go in to take their land, and you’ll take their land and live in it.

Once those nations have been destroyed ahead of you, watch out that you don’t get trapped into copying them. Don’t go asking about their gods, saying, “How did those nations serve their gods? I’ll do the same.”
Don’t worship Yahweh your God the way they worshiped their gods. They did every detestable thing Yahweh hates for their gods. They even burned their sons and daughters in the fire for them.
Be careful to do everything I command you. Don’t add anything to it or take anything away.
Suppose a prophet or someone who has prophetic dreams comes among you and gives you a sign or a wonder.
The sign or wonder they told you about comes true, and they say, “Let’s follow other gods,” gods you’ve never known, “and serve them.”
Don’t listen to that prophet or dreamer. Yahweh your God is testing you to see if you love him with your whole heart and your whole soul.
Follow Yahweh your God and honor him with reverence. Keep his commands, listen to his voice, serve him, and hold on to him.

That prophet or dreamer must be put to death for urging rebellion against Yahweh your God, who brought you out of Egypt and freed you from slavery. They tried to pull you off the path Yahweh your God told you to walk. That’s how you’ll remove the evil from among you.

Suppose your brother, your own mother’s son, or your son, daughter, the wife you hold close, or a friend as dear as your own life whispers to you, “Let’s go serve other gods,” gods neither you nor your ancestors have known.
They may be gods of the peoples around you, close by or far away, anywhere from one end of the earth to the other.
Don’t go along with that person or listen to them. Don’t pity them, spare them, or hide what they’ve done.
You must put that person to death. Your hand must be the first against them, followed by the hands of all the people.
Stone them to death because they tried to pull you away from Yahweh your God, who brought you out of Egypt, out of slavery.
All Israel will hear about it and be afraid to do anything that wicked among you again.
Suppose you hear a report about one of the towns Yahweh your God is giving you to live in.
You hear that some wicked people from among you have led the people of their town astray, saying, “Let’s go serve other gods,” gods you’ve never known.
Investigate it, ask questions, and check carefully. If the report is true and you know for sure that something this detestable happened among you,
put the people of that town to the sword. Destroy the town completely, along with everything in it, and put its livestock to the sword too.
Pile up everything taken from it in the middle of the street. Burn the town and everything taken from it for Yahweh your God. It must stay a heap of ruins forever and never be rebuilt.
Keep nothing that was marked for destruction. Then Yahweh will turn from his fierce anger, show you mercy and compassion, and grow your numbers, just as he swore to your ancestors.
He’ll do this when you listen to Yahweh your God, keep all the commands I’m giving you today, and do what’s right in his eyes.
You’re the children of Yahweh your God. When someone dies, don’t cut yourselves or shave a bald patch above your eyes for them.
You’re a people set apart as holy for Yahweh your God. Out of all the peoples on earth, he chose you to be his own.
Don’t eat anything detestable.
Here are the animals you can eat: cattle, sheep, goats,
deer, gazelles, roebucks, wild goats, ibexes, antelopes, and chamois.
You can eat an animal if its hoof is split all the way in two and it chews its cud.
Some animals chew their cud or have split hooves and are still off-limits. The camel, hare, and rabbit chew their cud but don’t have split hooves. They’re unclean to you.
The pig has a split hoof but doesn’t chew its cud. It’s unclean to you. Don’t eat the meat of any of these animals or touch their dead bodies.
Out of everything that lives in water, you can eat whatever has fins and scales.
Anything without fins and scales is unclean to you. Don’t eat it.
You can eat any clean bird.
Here are the ones you can’t eat: the eagle, the vulture, the osprey,
the red kite, the falcon, any kind of kite,
every kind of raven,
the ostrich, the owl, the seagull, any kind of hawk,
the little owl, the great owl, the horned owl,
the pelican, the vulture, the cormorant,
the stork, every kind of heron, the hoopoe, and the bat.
All winged crawling creatures are unclean to you. Don’t eat them.
You can eat any clean bird.

Don’t eat an animal that dies on its own. You can give it to a foreigner living in your town to eat, or sell it to a foreigner. You’re a people set apart as holy for Yahweh your God. Don’t boil a young goat in its mother’s milk.
Be sure to set aside a tenth of everything your fields produce from the seed you plant each year.

At the place Yahweh your God chooses for his name to dwell, eat before him the tenth of your grain, new wine, and oil, and the firstborn of your herds and flocks. That way you’ll learn to honor Yahweh your God with reverence all the time.
When Yahweh your God blesses you, the place he chooses for his name might be too far away for you to carry all of that there.
If so, sell it, take the money with you, and go to the place Yahweh your God chooses.
Spend the money on whatever you feel like having: cattle, sheep, wine, strong drink, whatever you want. Eat there before Yahweh your God, and celebrate with your household.
Don’t leave out the Levite in your town. The Levite has no share or inheritance with you.
At the end of every third year, bring that year’s whole tenth of what you produced and store it in your towns.

The Levite, who has no share or inheritance with you, and the foreigners, children without fathers, and widows living in your towns can come and eat their fill. Then Yahweh your God will bless everything you put your hands to.
At the end of every seven years, cancel debts.

Here’s how it works. Everyone who’s lent something to a neighbor must let that debt go. Don’t demand repayment from a neighbor who’s one of your own people, because Yahweh’s release has been announced.
You may demand repayment from a foreigner, but let go of whatever one of your own people owes you.
There won’t be anyone poor among you, because Yahweh will bless you in the land Yahweh your God is giving you to inherit,
if you listen carefully to Yahweh your God and follow everything I’m commanding you today.
Yahweh your God will bless you just as he promised. You’ll lend to many nations without having to borrow. You’ll rule over many nations, and they won’t rule over you.
If one of your own people is poor in any town in the land Yahweh your God is giving you, don’t harden your heart or close your hand to them.
Open your hand and lend them enough to cover what they need.

Watch out for this ugly thought: “The seventh year is almost here, when debts will be canceled.” Don’t look down on your poor neighbor and give them nothing. If they cry out to Yahweh against you, you’ll be guilty of sin.
Give to them freely, without resenting it in your heart. Yahweh your God will bless you for it in your work and in everything you put your hands to.
There will always be poor people in the land. That’s why I command you to open your hand to your own people who are in need or living in poverty.
If a fellow Hebrew, a man or a woman, is sold to you and serves you six years, set that person free in the seventh year.
When you let them go free, don’t send them away empty-handed.
Give them plenty from your flock, your threshing floor, and your winepress. Give to them out of what Yahweh your God has blessed you with.
Remember that you were a slave in Egypt, and Yahweh your God redeemed you. That’s why I’m giving you this command today.
But suppose the servant says, “I don’t want to leave you,” because they love you and your household and are doing well with you.
Then take an awl and push it through their ear into the door. They’ll be your servant for life. Do the same for a female servant.
Don’t begrudge setting them free. In six years of service they’ve given you twice the value of a hired worker. Yahweh your God will bless everything you do.
Set apart every firstborn male from your cattle and your flocks for Yahweh your God. Don’t put the firstborn of your cattle to work or shear the firstborn of your flock.
Every year you and your household will eat it before Yahweh your God in the place he chooses.
If it has a defect, whether it’s lame or blind or has any other defect, don’t sacrifice it to Yahweh your God.
Eat it in your own town. Clean and unclean people can both eat it, just as they can eat gazelle or deer.
Just don’t eat its blood. Pour it onto the ground like water.
Keep track of the month of Abib and celebrate Passover for Yahweh your God. It was in Abib that Yahweh your God brought you out of Egypt at night.
Offer Yahweh your God the Passover sacrifice from the flock or herd, at the place Yahweh chooses for his name to dwell.

Don’t eat bread made with yeast with it. For seven days eat bread made without yeast, the bread of hardship, because you left Egypt in a hurry. Remember the day you left Egypt for as long as you live.
For seven days there must be no yeast anywhere in your territory. Don’t leave any of the meat you sacrifice on the first evening overnight until morning.
You can’t offer the Passover sacrifice in just any town Yahweh your God gives you.
Offer it where Yahweh your God chooses for his name to dwell. Do it in the evening at sunset, at the time of year when you came out of Egypt.
Roast and eat it at the place Yahweh your God chooses. In the morning, head back to your tents.
Eat bread made without yeast for six days. On day seven, hold a solemn gathering for Yahweh your God. Do no work that day.
Count off seven weeks from the first time you put the sickle to the standing grain.
Celebrate the Festival of Weeks for Yahweh your God. Bring a gift you give freely, in keeping with how much Yahweh your God has blessed you.

Celebrate before Yahweh your God in the place he chooses for his name to dwell. Celebrate with your sons, daughters, male and female servants, and the Levites, foreigners, children without fathers, and widows who live among you.
Remember you were a slave in Egypt. Be careful to follow these laws.
Celebrate the Festival of Booths for seven days after bringing in what’s come from your threshing floor and your winepress.
Celebrate at your festival with your sons, daughters, male and female servants, and the Levites, foreigners, children without fathers, and widows in your towns.
Celebrate the festival for Yahweh your God for seven days at the place he chooses. Yahweh your God will bless your harvest and all your work, so you’ll be full of joy.

Three times a year all your males must appear before Yahweh your God at the place he chooses: at the Festival of Unleavened Bread, the Festival of Weeks, and the Festival of Booths. Nobody should show up before Yahweh empty-handed.
Each person should give what they can, in keeping with what Yahweh your God has given them.
Appoint judges and officers for your tribes in every town Yahweh your God gives you. They must judge the people fairly.
Don’t twist justice, play favorites, or take bribes. A bribe blinds even wise people and twists the words of people who do right.
Go after justice and nothing else, so you’ll live and inherit the land Yahweh your God gives you.
Don’t plant any tree as an Asherah beside the altar you build for Yahweh your God.
Don’t set up a sacred stone for yourselves either. Yahweh your God hates that.
Don’t sacrifice an ox or sheep to Yahweh your God if it has a defect or anything wrong with it. Yahweh your God finds that detestable.
Suppose you find a man or woman in one of the towns Yahweh your God gives you who breaks his covenant and does what’s evil in his eyes.
They’ve gone off to serve and bow down to other gods, or to the sun, moon, or any of the stars in the sky, something I never commanded.
When you hear about it, look into it carefully. If you find out for sure that such a detestable thing has happened in Israel,
bring the man or woman who did it out to your town gates and stone that person to death.
A death sentence requires the testimony of two or three witnesses. Nobody may be put to death on the testimony of just one witness.
The witnesses must be the first to act in putting the person to death, and afterward the rest of the people. That’s how you’ll remove the evil from among you.
If a dispute in your town is too hard for you to judge, whether it’s about a death, competing claims, or an injury, get up and go to the place Yahweh your God chooses.
Go to the Levitical priests and the judge serving at the time. Ask them about the case, and they’ll give you the verdict.
Follow the decision they give you from the place Yahweh chooses. Be careful to do everything they teach you.
Follow their instructions on the law and carry out the verdict they give you. Don’t turn away from their ruling to the right or to the left.
Anyone who defiantly refuses to listen to the priest serving there before Yahweh your God, or to the judge, must die. Remove that evil from Israel.
Everyone will hear about it and be afraid to act that defiantly again.
When you enter the land Yahweh your God gives you, settle there, and say, “I want a king over me like all the nations around me,”
make sure you appoint the king Yahweh your God chooses. Choose one of your own people as king. You may not put a foreigner who isn’t one of your own people over you.
The king must not build up a great stock of horses for himself or send the people back to Egypt to get more horses. Yahweh told you, “You must never go back that way.”
He must not take many wives for himself, or his heart will turn away. He must not pile up great stores of silver and gold for himself either.
When he takes his seat on the throne, he must write out his own copy of this law in a book, using the copy kept before the Levitical priests.
Keep it with him so he can read it all his life. That way he’ll learn to honor Yahweh his God with reverence and put every word of this law and these rules into practice.
Then he won’t think he’s above his own people or turn away from the command to the right or left. He and his children will reign a long time among the people of Israel.

The Levitical priests, along with the whole tribe of Levi, will have no share of the land or inheritance with Israel. They’ll eat from Yahweh’s offerings given through fire and from what belongs to him.
They’ll have no inheritance among their fellow Israelites. Yahweh is their inheritance, just as he told them.
Here’s the priests’ share from anyone who brings a sacrifice of an ox or a sheep: give the priest the shoulder, both cheeks, and the inner parts.
Give him the first of your grain, new wine, and oil, and the first wool you shear from your sheep.
Yahweh your God chose him out of all your tribes to stand and serve in Yahweh’s name, him and his sons forever.
If a Levite from any town in Israel where he lives wants with all his heart to go to the place Yahweh chooses,
he can serve in the name of Yahweh his God, just like his fellow Levites who stand there before Yahweh.
He’ll get the same share of food as they do, in addition to whatever he gets from selling his family property.
When you enter the land Yahweh your God gives you, don’t learn to copy the detestable practices of those nations.
Nobody among you may pass their son or daughter through the fire, practice divination, tell fortunes, cast spells, or practice sorcery.
Nobody may work charms, consult a familiar spirit, practice wizardry, or seek answers from the dead.
Yahweh finds anyone who does these things detestable. It’s because of these practices that Yahweh your God is driving those nations out ahead of you.
Be blameless before Yahweh your God.
The nations you’re taking the land from listen to sorcerers and diviners. Yahweh your God hasn’t given you permission to do that.
Yahweh your God will raise up a prophet like me from among your own people. Listen to him.
That’s what you asked Yahweh your God for at Horeb on the day you all gathered. You said, “Don’t let me hear Yahweh my God’s voice again or see this huge fire again, or I’ll die.”
Yahweh told me, “They’re right in what they’ve said.
I’ll raise up a prophet like you from among their own people. I’ll put my words in his mouth. He’ll tell them everything I command him.
If anyone refuses to listen to the words he speaks in my name, I’ll hold that person accountable.
But if a prophet dares to say something in my name that I never told him to say, or speaks in the name of other gods, that prophet must die.”
You might wonder, “How can we tell if Yahweh didn’t say something?”
If a prophet speaks in Yahweh’s name and what he says doesn’t come true, Yahweh didn’t say it. The prophet spoke on his own authority. Don’t be afraid of him.
When Yahweh your God cuts off the nations whose land he’s giving you, and you take their place and settle in their towns and homes,
set apart three towns in the middle of the land Yahweh your God is giving you to own.
Prepare the roads and divide the land Yahweh your God is giving you into three regions. That way anyone who kills someone can run to one of those towns.
Here’s who may run there and live: someone who kills a neighbor by accident and had never hated them before.

Say a person goes into the woods with a neighbor to chop wood. They swing the ax at a tree, but the ax head slips off the handle, hits the neighbor, and kills them. The person who swung the ax can run to one of those towns and live.

Otherwise the avenger of blood might chase after that person in a rage. If the road is too long, the avenger could catch them and kill them, even though they didn’t deserve to die because they never hated their neighbor.
That’s why I’m telling you to set apart three towns.
If Yahweh your God expands your borders as he swore to your ancestors and gives you all the land he promised them,
and you follow everything I’m commanding you today, loving Yahweh your God and always walking in his ways, add three more towns to those first three.
That way innocent blood won’t be shed in the land Yahweh your God gives you as an inheritance, and you won’t be guilty of bloodshed.
But suppose someone hates a neighbor, lies in wait, attacks and kills them, and then runs to one of those towns.
The elders of that person’s own town must send for them, bring them back, and hand them over to the avenger of blood to be put to death.
Don’t pity that person. Clear Israel of the guilt for innocent blood, so things will go well for you.
Don’t move your neighbor’s boundary marker. It was set there long ago in the land you’ll inherit, the land Yahweh your God is giving you to own.
One witness alone can’t establish that someone is guilty of a wrongdoing or a sin. It takes the testimony of two or three witnesses to establish the matter.
Suppose a dishonest witness comes forward and accuses someone of wrongdoing.
Both people in the dispute must stand before Yahweh, before the priests and judges serving at the time.
The judges must investigate carefully. If the witness has lied and given false testimony against their fellow Israelite,
do to the witness what they meant to do to the other person. That’s how you’ll remove the evil from among you.
The rest of the people will hear about it and be afraid to do anything that evil among you again.
Show no pity: life for life, eye for eye, tooth for tooth, hand for hand, foot for foot.
When you go out to battle and see your enemies’ horses, chariots, and an army bigger than yours, don’t be afraid of them. Yahweh your God, who brought you out of Egypt, is with you.
When you get close to the battle, the priest will step forward and speak to the people.
He’ll say, “Listen, Israel! Today you’re about to fight your enemies. Don’t lose heart. Don’t be afraid or tremble or let them terrify you.
Yahweh your God goes with you. He’ll fight for you against your enemies and save you.”
The officers will tell the people, “Has anyone built a new house and hasn’t dedicated it yet? Go home. If you die in battle, someone else will dedicate it.
Has anyone planted a vineyard and hasn’t enjoyed its fruit yet? Go home. If you die in battle, someone else will enjoy the fruit.
Is anyone engaged to a woman and hasn’t married her yet? Go home. If you die in battle, someone else will marry her.”
Then the officers will ask, “Is anyone afraid and losing heart? Go home, so your fear doesn’t make your brothers lose heart too.”
When the officers finish speaking, they’ll appoint commanders to lead the army.
When you approach a town to fight it, first offer it peace.
If the people accept and open the town to you, everyone there will be made to do forced labor and serve you.
If they refuse peace and go to war against you, lay siege to the town.
When Yahweh your God hands the town over to you, put every male in it to the sword.
Take the women, children, livestock, and everything in the town as spoils for yourselves. You may use what you take from the enemies Yahweh your God has handed over to you.
That’s how you’ll deal with towns far away, outside the towns of these nations here.
But in the towns of the peoples whose land Yahweh your God gives you as an inheritance, don’t leave anything alive that breathes.
Destroy them completely, the Hittites, Amorites, Canaanites, Perizzites, Hivites, and Jebusites, as Yahweh your God commanded.
Otherwise they’ll teach you to copy the detestable things they’ve done for their gods, and you’ll sin against Yahweh your God.

When you’ve laid siege to a town for a long time to capture it, don’t take an ax to its fruit trees. You can eat their fruit, so leave them standing. A tree in a field isn’t a person you can lay siege to.
You may cut down trees you know don’t produce food. Use them to build siegeworks against the town that’s fighting you until it falls.
Suppose someone is found killed, lying in a field in the land Yahweh your God is giving you to own, and nobody knows who struck them down.
Your elders and judges will go out and measure the distance from the body to the towns around it.
The elders of the town nearest the body will take a heifer from the herd that’s never done work or pulled a load under a yoke.
They’ll take her down to a valley with running water that’s never been plowed or planted. There in the valley they’ll break the heifer’s neck.
The Levitical priests will step forward. Yahweh your God chose them to serve him and bless people in his name. Their ruling settles every dispute and every case of assault.
All the elders of the town nearest the body will wash their hands over the heifer whose neck was broken in the valley.
They’ll say, “Our hands didn’t shed this blood, and our eyes didn’t see it happen.
Yahweh, forgive your people Israel, whom you redeemed. Don’t hold your people Israel guilty for the death of an innocent person.” Then they’ll be forgiven for the bloodshed.
That’s how you’ll clear yourselves of guilt for innocent blood by doing what’s right in Yahweh’s eyes.
When you go out to fight your enemies and Yahweh your God hands them over to you, and you take them captive,
you may see a beautiful woman among the captives, be drawn to her, and want to marry her.
Bring her into your home. She’ll shave her head and trim her nails.

She’ll take off the clothes she wore as a captive and stay in your house for a whole month to mourn her father and mother. After that, you may sleep with her and become her husband, and she’ll be your wife.
If you’re no longer pleased with her, let her go wherever she wants. You must never sell her for money or treat her like a slave, because you’ve humiliated her.
Suppose a man has two wives, one he loves and one he hates. Both have children with him, and his firstborn son belongs to the wife he hates.
When he divides what he owns among his sons, he must not give the rights of the firstborn to the son of the wife he loves ahead of his actual firstborn, the son of the wife he hates.

He must recognize the son of the wife he hates as his firstborn by giving him a double share of everything he owns. That son is the first sign of his strength, and the rights of the firstborn are his.
Suppose a man has a stubborn, rebellious son who won’t obey his father or mother. Even after they discipline him, he won’t listen.
His father and mother must take hold of him and bring him out to the elders at the gate of his town.
They’ll tell the elders, “This son of ours is stubborn and rebellious. He won’t listen to us. He’s a glutton and a drunk.”
All the men of his town will stone him to death. That’s how you’ll remove the evil from among you. All Israel will hear and be afraid.
If a man commits a sin that deserves death, is put to death, and is hung on a tree,
don’t leave his body hanging there overnight. Bury him that same day, because anyone hung on a tree is under God’s curse. Don’t defile the land Yahweh your God is giving you as an inheritance.
If you see your fellow Israelite’s ox or sheep wandering off, don’t look the other way. Bring it back to them.
If the owner lives far away or you don’t know whose animal it is, take it home and keep it until the owner comes looking for it. Then give it back.
Do the same for a donkey, a piece of clothing, or anything else someone loses and you find. Don’t look the other way.
If you see your fellow Israelite’s donkey or ox collapsed by the road, don’t walk past it. Help them get it back on its feet.
A woman must not wear men’s clothes, and a man must not put on women’s clothes. Yahweh your God finds it detestable when anyone does that.
If you come across a bird’s nest in a tree or on the ground and the mother is sitting on chicks or eggs, don’t take the mother with the young.
Let the mother go. You can take the young for yourself. Then things will go well for you and you’ll live long.
When you build a new house, put a railing around the roof. That way you won’t bring guilt on your household if someone falls from there.
Don’t plant two kinds of seed in your vineyard. If you do, both the crop you planted and the produce of the vineyard will be defiled.
Don’t hitch an ox and a donkey together to plow.
Don’t wear clothes woven with wool and linen together.
Put tassels on the four corners of the cloak you wrap around yourself.
Suppose a man marries a woman, sleeps with her, and then hates her.
He brings shameful accusations against her and ruins her good name, saying, “I married this woman, but when I slept with her, I found no evidence of her virginity.”
The young woman’s father and mother will bring the evidence of her virginity to the town elders at the gate.
Her father will tell the elders, “I gave my daughter to this man as his wife, and he hates her.

Now he’s made this shameful accusation: ‘I found no evidence that your daughter was a virgin.’ Here’s the evidence of my daughter’s virginity.” They’ll spread the cloth out in front of the town elders.
The elders will take the man and discipline him.

They’ll fine him a hundred silver shekels and give the money to the young woman’s father, because the man ruined the good name of a virgin in Israel. She’ll remain his wife, and he can never divorce her.
But if the accusation is true and no evidence of her virginity is found,

bring the young woman to the entrance of her father’s house. The men of her town will stone her to death, because she did a disgraceful thing in Israel by acting like a prostitute in her father’s house. That’s how you’ll remove the evil from among you.
If a man is found sleeping with another man’s wife, both the man who slept with her and the woman must die. That’s how you’ll remove the evil from Israel.
Suppose a young woman who’s a virgin is engaged to be married, and a man finds her in town and sleeps with her.
Take both of them out to the town gate and stone them to death. She didn’t cry out while she was in town, and he violated his neighbor’s wife. That’s how you’ll remove the evil from among you.
But if the man finds an engaged woman out in the field and forces her to have sex with him, only the man who raped her must die.
Do nothing to the woman. She hasn’t committed a sin that deserves death. This is like someone attacking and killing their neighbor.
He found her out in the field. The engaged woman cried out, and nobody was there to save her.
If a man finds a virgin who isn’t engaged, grabs her and sleeps with her, and they’re discovered,
the man who slept with her must pay her father fifty silver shekels. She’ll become his wife because he violated her. He can never divorce her.
A man must not take his father’s wife. He must not uncover his father’s garment.
A man whose genitals have been crushed or cut off may not enter Yahweh’s assembly.
Someone born from a forbidden union may not enter Yahweh’s assembly. None of their descendants may enter, even to the tenth generation.
No Ammonite or Moabite may enter Yahweh’s assembly. None of their descendants may enter, even to the tenth generation, for all time.
They didn’t meet you with bread and water on the road out of Egypt. They also hired Balaam son of Beor from Pethor in Mesopotamia to curse you.
Yahweh your God refused to listen to Balaam. He turned the curse into a blessing for you because he loved you.
Don’t seek their peace or prosperity for as long as you live.
Don’t despise an Edomite. They’re your relatives. Don’t despise an Egyptian either, because you lived as a foreigner in their land.
Their children in the third generation may enter Yahweh’s assembly.
When you camp out against your enemies, keep yourselves away from every evil thing.
If a man becomes unclean because of something that happens during the night, he must go outside the camp and stay out.
When evening comes, he’ll bathe in water. After sunset he can come back into camp.
Set aside a place outside the camp where you can go to relieve yourselves.
Carry a trowel with your gear. When you relieve yourself, use it to dig a hole, then cover up what you left.
Yahweh your God walks through the middle of your camp to rescue you and hand your enemies over to you. Keep the camp holy so he doesn’t see anything unclean among you and turn away.
If an enslaved person escapes from their master and comes to you, don’t hand them back.
Let them live among you in whichever town they choose, wherever they’re most comfortable. Don’t mistreat them.
No Israelite woman or man is to serve as a shrine prostitute.
Don’t bring the pay of a female or male prostitute into the house of Yahweh your God to fulfill a vow. Yahweh your God finds both detestable.
Don’t charge a fellow Israelite interest on a loan, whether it’s money, food, or anything else people lend at interest.
You can charge a foreigner interest, but don’t charge your fellow Israelites. Then Yahweh your God will bless everything you put your hands to in the land you’re going to possess.
When you make a vow to Yahweh your God, don’t drag your feet about keeping it. Yahweh your God will require it of you, and you’ll be guilty of sin if you fail to do it.
If you choose to make no vow, you haven’t sinned.
Keep the promises you’ve spoken. When you freely make a vow to Yahweh your God, do what you said you’d do.
When you step into your neighbor’s vineyard, eat as many grapes as you want until you’re full. Don’t put any in a container to take away.
When you go into your neighbor’s standing grain, you can pick heads of grain by hand. Don’t take a sickle to their crop.

Suppose a man marries a woman and then decides he no longer wants her because he’s found something indecent in her. He writes her a certificate of divorce, puts it in her hand, and sends her out of his house.
After she leaves his house, she may go and marry another man.
