Suppose her second husband hates her and writes her a certificate of divorce, puts it in her hand, and sends her away, or suppose that husband dies.
The first husband who sent her away can’t marry her again after she’s been defiled. Yahweh finds that detestable. Don’t bring sin on the land Yahweh your God is giving you as an inheritance.
When a man has just married, don’t send him out with the army or assign him any other public duty. Let him stay home for a year and bring joy to the wife he married.
Don’t take someone’s mill or upper millstone as security for a loan. That’s taking their livelihood as security.
If someone is caught kidnapping a fellow Israelite and treating them as a slave or selling them, the kidnapper must die. That’s how you’ll remove the evil from among you.
When a case of leprosy turns up, take care to follow everything the Levitical priests teach you. Do exactly what I told them.
Remember what Yahweh your God did to Miriam on the road out of Egypt.
When you lend your neighbor anything, don’t go into their house to take their pledge.
Stand outside and let the person you’re lending to bring the pledge out to you.
If they’re poor, don’t keep what they pledged overnight.
Give it back by sunset so they can sleep in their cloak and bless you. Yahweh your God will count that as righteousness for you.
Don’t take advantage of a hired worker who’s poor and in need, whether they’re a fellow Israelite or a foreigner living in one of your towns.
Pay them that day, before sunset. They’re poor and counting on that money. If they cry out to Yahweh against you, you’ll be guilty of sin.
Parents must not be put to death for what their children did, and children must not be put to death for what their parents did. A person may be put to death only for their own sin.
Don’t deny justice to a foreigner or a child without a father, and don’t take a widow’s clothing as security for a loan.
Remember that you were a slave in Egypt and Yahweh your God redeemed you there. That’s why I’m telling you to do this.

When you harvest your field and forget a bundle of grain, don’t go back for it. Leave it for the foreigner, the child without a father, and the widow, so Yahweh your God will bless all the work you do.
When you beat the branches of your olive tree to harvest it, don’t go back over them. Leave what’s still there for the foreigner, the child without a father, and the widow.
When you pick grapes from your vineyard, don’t go back for what you missed. Leave it for the foreigner, the child without a father, and the widow.
Remember that you were a slave in Egypt. That’s why I’m telling you to do this.
When people have a dispute and take it to court, the judges are to clear the person in the right and condemn the one in the wrong.
If the guilty person deserves a beating, the judge must have him lie down and be beaten in front of him. The number of lashes must fit the offense.
The judge may order up to forty lashes. Any more than that would humiliate your fellow Israelite in front of you.
Don't muzzle an ox while it's threshing grain.
If brothers live together and one dies without a son, his widow must not marry someone outside the family. Her husband's brother is to marry her and fulfill his duty to her as her brother-in-law.
The first child she bears will carry on the dead brother's name so that his name won't disappear from Israel.

If the man doesn't want to marry his brother's widow, she is to go to the elders at the town gate and say, “My husband's brother refuses to carry on his brother's name in Israel. He won't fulfill his duty to me as my brother-in-law.”
The elders of his town must call him in and talk to him. If he stands his ground and says, “I don't want to marry her,”

his brother's widow is to go up to him in front of the elders, take the sandal off his foot, and spit in his face. She must say, “This is what happens to the man who won't build up his brother's family.”
From then on, his family will be known in Israel as “the family of the man whose sandal was removed.”
If two men are fighting and the wife of one steps in to save her husband from the man beating him, and she reaches out and grabs that man by his genitals,
you must cut off her hand. Show no pity.
Don't carry two different weights in your bag, one heavy and one light.
Don't keep two different measures at home, one large and one small.
Use weights and measures that are accurate and fair, so you'll live a long time in the land the LORD your God is giving you.
The LORD your God detests everyone who cheats like this and everyone who acts dishonestly.
Remember what Amalek did to you on the road when you came out of Egypt.
They met you on the road while you were worn out and attacked the weak people lagging at the back. They had no fear of God.
When the LORD your God gives you rest from all the enemies around you in the land he's giving you as your own, wipe out the memory of Amalek from under the sky. Don't forget.
When you enter the land the LORD your God is giving you as your inheritance, take possession of it, and settle there,
take some of the first produce you harvest from the land the LORD your God is giving you. Put it in a basket and go to the place the LORD your God chooses for his name to dwell.
Go to the priest serving at that time and tell him, “Today I declare to the LORD your God that I've come into the land the LORD swore to our ancestors he would give us.”
The priest is to take the basket from your hand and set it down in front of the altar of the LORD your God.

Then say in the presence of the LORD your God, “My ancestor was a Syrian on the verge of dying. He went down to Egypt and lived there with only a few people. There his family grew into a great, powerful nation with many people.
The Egyptians mistreated us, made us suffer, and forced us to do hard labor.
Then we cried out to the LORD, the God of our ancestors. The LORD heard us and saw how we were suffering, how hard we were working, and how badly we were oppressed.
The LORD brought us out of Egypt with a mighty hand and an outstretched arm, with terrifying acts, signs, and wonders.
He brought us here and gave us this land, a land flowing with milk and honey.
And now I've brought the first produce from the land you gave me, LORD.” Set it down before the LORD your God and worship there in his presence.
Celebrate all the good things the LORD your God has given you and your household. Include the Levites and the foreigners living among you in the celebration.

The third year is the year of the tithe. When you've finished setting aside a tenth of all you produced that year, give it to the Levites, the foreigners, the fatherless, and the widows, so they can eat their fill in your towns.

Then say in the presence of the LORD your God, “I've taken what was set apart for you out of my house and given it to the Levites, the foreigners, the fatherless, and the widows, just as you commanded me. I haven't broken or forgotten any of your commands.
I haven't eaten any of it while I was mourning, taken any of it out while I was unclean, or given any of it for the dead. I've listened to the LORD my God and done everything you commanded me.
Look down from your holy home in heaven and bless your people Israel and the land you've given us, a land flowing with milk and honey, just as you swore to our ancestors.”
Today the LORD your God commands you to follow these laws and rulings. Keep them and live by them with all your heart and all your soul.
Today you've declared that the LORD is your God. You've committed to following his ways, keeping his laws, commands, and rulings, and listening to his voice.
Today the LORD has declared that you are his own people, just as he promised you, and that you are to keep all his commands.
He will set you high above every nation he has made and give you praise, a good name, and honor. You will be a people set apart for the LORD your God, just as he said.
Moses and the elders of Israel told the people, “Keep all the commands I'm giving you today.
On the day you cross the Jordan into the land the LORD your God is giving you, set up some large stones and coat them with plaster.

Once you've crossed, write every word of this law on the stones, so you can enter the land the LORD your God is giving you. It's a land flowing with milk and honey, just as the LORD, the God of your ancestors, promised you.
After you cross the Jordan, set up these stones on Mount Ebal as I'm telling you today, and coat them with plaster.
Build a stone altar there for the LORD your God. Don't use any iron tool on the stones.
Build the altar of the LORD your God out of uncut stones and offer burnt offerings on it to the LORD your God.
Make peace offerings, eat there, and celebrate in the presence of the LORD your God.
Write every word of this law clearly on the stones.”
Moses and the Levitical priests told all Israel, “Be quiet and listen, Israel! Today you've become the people of the LORD your God.
So listen to the LORD your God and follow the commands and laws I'm giving you today.”
That same day Moses gave the people these instructions.
“After you cross the Jordan, Simeon, Levi, Judah, Issachar, Joseph, and Benjamin will stand on Mount Gerizim to bless the people.
Reuben, Gad, Asher, Zebulun, Dan, and Naphtali will stand on Mount Ebal for the curse.
The Levites must call out in a loud voice to all the men of Israel,
‘Cursed is anyone who makes a carved or cast idol and sets it up in secret. A craftsman made it by hand, and the LORD detests it.’ All the people must answer, ‘Amen.’
‘Cursed is anyone who dishonors their father or mother.’ All the people must say, ‘Amen.’
‘Cursed is anyone who moves their neighbor's boundary marker.’ All the people must say, ‘Amen.’
‘Cursed is anyone who leads a blind person off course on the road.’ All the people must say, ‘Amen.’
‘Cursed is anyone who denies justice to a foreigner, a fatherless child, or a widow.’ All the people must say, ‘Amen.’
‘Cursed is anyone who sleeps with his father's wife, because he dishonors his father's bed.’ All the people must say, ‘Amen.’
‘Cursed is anyone who has sex with any animal.’ All the people must say, ‘Amen.’
‘Cursed is anyone who sleeps with his sister, whether she's his father's daughter or his mother's daughter.’ All the people must say, ‘Amen.’
‘Cursed is anyone who sleeps with his mother-in-law.’ All the people must say, ‘Amen.’
‘Cursed is anyone who kills their neighbor in secret.’ All the people must say, ‘Amen.’
‘Cursed is anyone who takes a bribe to kill an innocent person.’ All the people must say, ‘Amen.’
‘Cursed is anyone who fails to uphold the words of this law by putting them into practice.’ All the people must say, ‘Amen.’”
If you listen closely to the LORD your God and carefully follow every command I'm giving you today, the LORD your God will set you high above every nation on earth.
If you listen to the LORD your God, all these blessings will come your way and catch up with you.
You'll be blessed in the city and in the fields.
Your children, your crops, and your animals will be blessed, including the young of your herds and flocks.
Your basket and your kneading bowl will be blessed.
You'll be blessed when you come in and when you go out.
The LORD will defeat the enemies who rise up against you. They'll come at you from one direction and run away in seven.
The LORD will command a blessing on your barns and everything you put your hands to. He'll bless you in the land the LORD your God is giving you.
If you keep the commands of the LORD your God and follow his ways, he'll establish you as his own holy people, just as he swore to you.
All the peoples on earth will see that you bear the LORD's name, and they'll be afraid of you.
The LORD will give you plenty of children, livestock, and crops in the land he swore to your ancestors he would give you.
The LORD will open up his rich storehouse in the sky to send rain on your land at the right time and bless all your work. You'll lend to many nations without having to borrow.
The LORD will make you the head instead of the tail. You'll always be on top if you listen to the commands of the LORD your God that I'm giving you today and follow them carefully.
Don't turn away from anything I'm commanding you today, to the right or to the left, to follow and serve other gods.
But if you refuse to listen to the LORD your God and fail to follow all his commands and laws I'm giving you today, all these curses will come after you and catch up with you.
You'll be cursed in the city and in the fields.
Your basket and your kneading bowl will be cursed.
Your children, your crops, and the young of your herds and flocks will be cursed.
You'll be cursed when you come in and when you go out.
The LORD will send curses, confusion, and rebuke on everything you try to do. You'll be destroyed and perish quickly because you abandoned me by doing evil.
The LORD will make disease stick to you until he wipes you out of the land you're entering to take over.
The LORD will strike you with wasting disease, fever, inflammation, scorching heat, the sword, crop blight, and mildew. They'll chase you until you perish.
The sky above you will be like bronze, and the ground beneath you like iron.
The LORD will turn your land's rain into powder and dust. It will fall from the sky until you're destroyed.
The LORD will let your enemies defeat you. You'll go out against them from one direction and run away in seven. You'll be tossed around among all the kingdoms on earth.
Your bodies will become food for the birds and wild animals, with nobody to scare them away.
The LORD will strike you with the boils of Egypt, tumors, scurvy, and itching that you can't get rid of.
The LORD will strike you with madness, blindness, and confusion.
You'll feel your way around at noon like a blind person in the dark. Nothing you try will go well. You'll be oppressed and robbed all the time, with nobody to rescue you.
You'll get engaged, but another man will sleep with the woman you were going to marry. You'll build a house and never live in it. You'll plant a vineyard and never enjoy its fruit.

Your ox will be killed right in front of you, and you won't eat any of it. Your donkey will be taken by force before your eyes and never returned. Your sheep will be handed over to your enemies, and nobody will rescue you.
Your sons and daughters will be handed over to another people. You'll wear out your eyes looking for them all day, longing for them and powerless to do anything.
A nation you've never known will eat everything you grow and take everything you've worked for. You'll be oppressed and crushed all the time,
until what you see with your own eyes drives you mad.
The LORD will strike your knees and legs with painful boils that can't be healed. They'll cover you from the soles of your feet to the top of your head.
The LORD will take you and the king you appoint to a nation neither you nor your ancestors ever knew. There you'll serve other gods made of wood and stone.
You'll become a shocking sight, a cautionary saying, and a name people throw around wherever the LORD takes you.
You'll scatter plenty of seed in the fields and harvest hardly anything, because locusts will devour it.
You'll plant and tend vineyards, but you won't drink their wine or gather the grapes, because worms will eat them.
You'll have olive trees all across your land, but you won't rub any of their oil on yourself, because the olives will fall off.
You'll have sons and daughters, but you won't get to keep them, because they'll be taken captive.
Locusts will devour all your trees and everything your land grows.
The foreigners living among you will rise higher and higher above you, while you sink lower and lower.
They'll lend to you, and you won't lend to them. They'll be the head, and you'll be the tail.
All these curses will come after you, chase you down, and catch you until you're destroyed, because you refused to listen to the LORD your God and follow the commands and laws he gave you.
They'll be a sign and a wonder to you and your descendants forever.
You had plenty of everything, yet you didn't serve the LORD your God joyfully and with a glad heart.
So you'll serve the enemies the LORD sends against you, hungry, thirsty, naked, and lacking everything. He'll put an iron yoke around your neck until he destroys you.
The LORD will bring a nation against you from the far end of the earth. It'll swoop down like an eagle, and you won't understand its language.
It's a fierce-looking nation that shows no respect to the elderly and no kindness to the young.
They'll eat your livestock and crops until you're destroyed. They won't leave you any grain, new wine, oil, calves, or lambs until they've brought you to ruin.
They'll surround all your towns until the high, fortified walls you trusted come down. They'll lay siege to every town throughout the land the LORD your God gave you.
Your enemies will put you under such pressure during the siege that you'll eat the flesh of your own sons and daughters, the children the LORD your God gave you.
Even the gentlest, most delicate man among you will look with hostility at his brother, the wife he loves, and the children he has left.
He won't share any of the flesh of the children he's eating with any of them, because he has nothing else left under the pressure of the siege your enemy lays against all your towns.
Even the gentlest, most delicate woman among you, who was too delicate to put her bare foot on the ground, will look with hostility at the husband she loves, her son, and her daughter,

and at the newborn who comes from between her feet and the children she bears. She'll eat them in secret because she has nothing left under the pressure of the siege your enemy lays against your towns.
If you fail to follow every word of this law written in this book and fail to honor this glorious and awe-inspiring name, the LORD your God,
the LORD will send terrifying plagues on you and your descendants, devastating plagues and severe sicknesses that go on and on.
He'll bring back all the diseases of Egypt that you dreaded, and they'll stick to you.
The LORD will even bring on you every sickness and plague this book of the law doesn't mention, until you're destroyed.
You were once as numerous as the stars in the sky, but only a few of you will be left, because you refused to listen to the LORD your God.
Just as the LORD took joy in doing you good and making you numerous, the LORD will take joy in bringing you to ruin and destroying you. You'll be uprooted from the land you're going in to possess.
The LORD will scatter you among all peoples from one end of the earth to the other. There you'll serve gods of wood and stone that neither you nor your ancestors ever knew.
Among those nations you'll find no peace and nowhere to rest your feet. There the LORD will give you a trembling heart, failing eyes, and a soul worn out by longing.
Your life will hang in the balance. You'll be afraid night and day, with no certainty that you'll live.
In the morning you'll say, “I wish it were evening!” At evening you'll say, “I wish it were morning!” That's how terrified you'll be because of what you see.
The LORD will send you back to Egypt in ships, along the route I told you you'd never see again. There you'll offer yourselves to your enemies as slaves, men and women alike, but nobody will buy you.
These are the terms of the covenant the LORD told Moses to make with the Israelites in Moab, alongside the covenant he had made with them at Horeb.
Moses called all Israel together and said, “You saw for yourselves everything the LORD did in Egypt to Pharaoh, his servants, and his whole land.
You saw the great trials, the signs, and those incredible wonders with your own eyes.
Yet to this day the LORD hasn't given you a heart that understands, eyes that see, or ears that hear.
I led you through the wilderness for forty years. The clothes on your backs and the sandals on your feet never wore out.
You didn't eat bread or drink wine or any strong drink, so you'd know that I am the LORD your God.
When you reached this place, King Sihon of Heshbon and King Og of Bashan came out to fight us, and we defeated them.
We took their land and gave it as an inheritance to the tribes of Reuben and Gad and half the tribe of Manasseh.
So keep the terms of this covenant and put them into practice, so things will go well in everything you do.
Today all of you are standing in the presence of the LORD your God: your leaders, your tribes, your elders, your officers, and every man of Israel,
along with your children, your wives, and the foreigners in your camps, from those who cut your wood to those who draw your water.
You're here to enter the covenant of the LORD your God and bind yourselves by the oath he's making with you today.
Today he's establishing you as his people and becoming your God, just as he told you and swore to your ancestors Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob.
I'm making this covenant and oath with more than just you.
It includes those standing here with us today before the LORD our God and those who aren't here with us today.
You know how we lived in Egypt and how we traveled right through the other nations along the way.
You saw the detestable things among them, their idols made of wood, stone, silver, and gold.
So make sure no man, woman, family, or tribe among you turns their heart away from the LORD our God today to serve those nations' gods. Don't let a root that produces bitter poison grow among you.
Someone might hear the words of this curse and tell themselves, ‘I'll be fine even if I stubbornly go my own way.’ That would bring ruin to the well-watered land along with the dry.
The LORD won't pardon that person. The LORD's anger and jealousy will blaze against them, every curse written in this book will fall on them, and the LORD will erase their name from under the sky.
The LORD will single them out from all the tribes of Israel for disaster, in keeping with every curse of the covenant written in this book of the law.
The next generation, your children who come after you, and foreigners who come from far away will see the plagues in the land and the sickness the LORD has inflicted on it.

They'll see the whole land burning with sulfur and covered with salt. Nothing is planted, nothing grows, and even grass can't sprout. It'll be like Sodom, Gomorrah, Admah, and Zeboiim when the LORD overturned those cities in his fierce anger.
All the nations will ask, ‘Why did the LORD do this to this land? What stirred up such fierce anger?’
People will answer, ‘They abandoned the covenant of the LORD, the God of their ancestors, that he made with them when he brought them out of Egypt.
They went off to serve and worship other gods, gods they didn't know and that he hadn't given them.
So the LORD's anger burned against this land, and he brought on it every curse written in this book.
In furious anger the LORD ripped them out of their land by the roots and threw them into another land, where they are today.’
Things kept secret belong to the LORD our God. What he's revealed belongs to us and our children forever, so we can live by every word of this law.”
When all these things happen to you, the blessing and the curse I've set before you, remember them wherever the LORD your God has driven you among the nations.
Then you and your children will return to the LORD your God and listen to him with all your heart and all your soul, doing everything I'm commanding you today.
Then the LORD your God will free you from captivity, have compassion on you, and gather you back from all the peoples where he scattered you.
Even if your people have been driven to the farthest reaches under heaven, the LORD your God will gather you from there and bring you back.
The LORD your God will bring you into the land your ancestors owned, and it'll be yours. He'll do good to you and make you more numerous than your ancestors.
The LORD your God will circumcise your hearts and your descendants' hearts, so you'll love the LORD your God with all your heart and all your soul and live.
The LORD your God will put all these curses on your enemies, the people who hated and persecuted you.
You'll return and listen to the LORD and follow every command I'm giving you today.

The LORD your God will make all your work flourish and give you many children, thriving livestock, and abundant crops. The LORD will once again take joy in doing good for you, just as he took joy in doing good for your ancestors,
if you listen to the LORD your God, keep the commands and laws written in this book of the law, and turn to the LORD your God with all your heart and all your soul.
This command I'm giving you today is within your ability and within your reach.
It isn't up in heaven, where you'd have to ask, “Who'll go up to heaven for us, bring it back, and tell us what it says so we can do it?”
It isn't across the sea either, where you'd have to ask, “Who'll cross the sea for us, bring it back, and tell us what it says so we can do it?”
The word is right here with you, in your mouth and in your heart, so you can put it into practice.
Look, today I've put life and prosperity before you, along with death and disaster.

Today I'm commanding you to love the LORD your God, follow his ways, and keep his commands, laws, and rulings. Then you'll live and grow in number, and the LORD your God will bless you in the land you're going in to take as your own.
But if your heart turns away and you refuse to listen, and you let yourself be drawn away to worship and serve other gods,
I declare to you today that you'll certainly perish. You won't live long in the land you're crossing the Jordan to take as your own.
Today I call heaven and earth as witnesses against you. I've set life and death before you, the blessing and the curse. Choose life, so you and your descendants can live.

Love the LORD your God, listen to his voice, and hold on to him. He is your life and the one who gives you long days, so you can live in the land the LORD swore to give your ancestors Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob.
Moses went and said these words to all Israel.
“I'm 120 years old today. I can't go out and come in anymore. The LORD has told me, ‘You won't cross this Jordan.’
The LORD your God himself will cross ahead of you. He'll destroy these nations before you, and you'll take possession of their land. Joshua will cross ahead of you, just as the LORD said.
The LORD will do to them what he did to Sihon and Og, the Amorite kings, and to their land when he destroyed them.
The LORD will hand them over to you, and you'll deal with them according to every command I've given you.
Be strong and brave. Don't let them scare or terrify you, because the LORD your God himself goes with you. He won't fail you or leave you.”

Moses called Joshua and said in front of all Israel, “Be strong and brave. You're going with these people into the land the LORD swore to give their ancestors, and you'll lead them into their inheritance.
The LORD himself goes ahead of you. He'll be with you and won't fail you or leave you. Don't be afraid. Don't lose heart.”
Moses wrote down this law and gave it to the priests from the tribe of Levi who carried the ark of the LORD's covenant, and to all the elders of Israel.
Moses gave them this command: “At the end of every seven years, at the appointed time in the year of release, during the Festival of Booths,
when all Israel comes to appear before the LORD your God at the place he chooses, read this law out loud so everyone can hear.
Bring everyone together: men, women, children, and the foreigners in your towns. Let them hear and learn to honor the LORD your God and carefully follow every word of this law.
Then their children who haven't learned it yet will hear and learn to honor the LORD your God for as long as you live in the land you're crossing the Jordan to take as your own.”

The LORD said to Moses, “Your time to die is near. Call Joshua and come with him to the Tent of Meeting so I can commission him.” So Moses and Joshua went and presented themselves at the Tent of Meeting.
The LORD appeared at the tent in a pillar of cloud, and the pillar stood over the entrance.

The LORD told Moses, “You'll soon die and rest with your ancestors. These people will be unfaithful to me and chase after the foreign gods of the land they're entering. They'll abandon me and break the covenant I made with them.

Then my anger will flare up against them. I'll abandon them and hide my face from them. They'll be devoured, and all sorts of trouble and disaster will come upon them. Then they'll say, ‘Aren't these disasters happening because our God isn't with us?’
I will certainly hide my face that day because of all the evil they've done by turning to other gods.
So write down this song for yourselves and teach it to the Israelites. Put it on their lips, so the song can be my witness against them.

I'll bring them into the land flowing with milk and honey that I swore to give their ancestors. They'll eat their fill and grow fat. Then they'll turn to other gods and serve them, treat me with contempt, and break my covenant.

When all sorts of trouble and disaster come upon them, this song will testify as a witness before them. Their descendants will still remember its words. I know the direction they're headed and what they're doing today, before I've even brought them into the land I promised them.”
That same day Moses wrote down the song and taught it to the Israelites.
The LORD commissioned Joshua son of Nun and said, “Be strong and brave. You'll bring the Israelites into the land I swore to give them. I'll be with you.”
When Moses had finished writing every word of this law in a book,
he gave this command to the Levites who carried the ark of the LORD's covenant:
“Take this book of the law and put it beside the ark of the covenant of the LORD your God. Keep it there as a witness against you.
I know how rebellious and stubborn you are. You've rebelled against the LORD while I'm still alive here with you. How much more will you rebel after I'm gone?
Bring all your tribal elders and officers to me. I'll say these words so they can hear them, and I'll call heaven and earth as witnesses against them.

I know that after I die you'll completely corrupt yourselves and turn away from the path I told you to follow. In the days to come, disaster will reach you because you'll do evil in the LORD's sight and stir up his anger with what your hands have made.”
Then Moses recited every word of this song so the whole assembly of Israel could hear it.
Listen, heavens, and I'll speak. Let the earth hear what I have to say.
Let my teaching fall like rain and my words settle like dew, like a mist over tender grass and showers over green plants.
I'll proclaim the LORD's name. Give our God the praise his greatness deserves!
He is the Rock. Everything he does is perfect, and all his ways are fair. He's faithful and does no wrong. He's just and upright.
They acted dishonestly toward him. Their own corruption shows they're no longer his children. They're a twisted and crooked generation.
Is this how you repay the LORD, you foolish people with no sense? Isn't he your Father, the one who bought you, made you, and established you?
Remember the old days. Think back through the generations. Ask your father, and he'll explain. Ask your elders, and they'll tell you.
When the Most High handed out land to the nations and separated the human race, he set the peoples' boundaries according to the number of the Israelites.
The LORD's share is his people. Jacob is the inheritance that belongs to him.
He found Jacob in a desert, in a barren wilderness where the wind howled. He surrounded him, cared for him, and guarded him like the pupil of his own eye.
Like an eagle stirring up her nest and hovering over her young, the LORD spread his wings, caught them, and carried them on his feathers.
The LORD alone led Jacob. No foreign god was with him.
He let him ride over the heights of the earth and eat what the fields produced. He gave him honey from rock and oil from flint,
butter from his cattle and milk from his flock, fat from lambs, the rams of Bashan and goats, and the finest wheat. You drank wine, the blood of the grape.
But Jeshurun grew fat and kicked. You grew fat, thick, and sleek. Then he abandoned the God who made him and rejected the Rock who saved him.
They stirred up his jealousy with foreign gods and made him angry with detestable things.
They sacrificed to demons instead of God, to gods they'd never known, new gods that had just shown up and that their ancestors had never feared.
You stopped thinking about the Rock who fathered you. You forgot the God who gave you birth.
The LORD saw what his sons and daughters were doing to provoke him and recoiled in disgust.
He said, “I'll hide my face from them and see how they end up. They're a twisted generation, children with no faithfulness.
They made me jealous with something that isn't God and provoked me with worthless idols. I'll make them jealous with people who don't even count as a nation. I'll provoke them with a foolish nation.
My anger has started a fire that burns down to the depths of Sheol. It consumes the earth and what it produces and sets the roots of the mountains on fire.
I'll pile disasters on them and use up my arrows against them.
Hunger will waste them away. Burning heat and bitter destruction will consume them. I'll send beasts to bite them and the venom of vipers that slide through the dust.
Outside, the sword will take their loved ones. Inside their rooms, terror will strike young men and young women, nursing babies and gray-haired men alike.
I said I'd scatter them far away and wipe out their memory from among humanity.
But I held back for fear the enemy would take it the wrong way and boast, ‘Our hand is mighty. The LORD had nothing to do with this.’”
They're a nation with no good judgment. There's no understanding in them.
If only they were wise enough to understand this and think about how it will end for them!
How could one person chase a thousand or two put ten thousand to flight unless their Rock had sold them and the LORD had handed them over?
Their rock can't compare to our Rock. Even our enemies admit it.
Their vine comes from Sodom's vine and Gomorrah's fields. Their grapes are poisonous and their clusters bitter.
Their wine is snake poison, the cruel venom of deadly snakes.
“Isn't all this stored away with me, sealed up among my treasures?
Vengeance and repayment are mine. Their time will come when their feet slip. Their day of disaster is close, and their ruin is rushing toward them.”
The LORD will judge his people and have compassion on his servants when he sees their strength is gone and no one remains, confined or free.
He'll ask, “Where are their gods now? Where's the rock they ran to for shelter?
Where are the gods that ate the fat of their sacrifices and drank the wine of their offerings? Let those gods get up and help you. Let them protect you!
See now that I myself am God. There's no god beside me. I take life and give life. I wound and I heal. Nobody can rescue anyone from my hand.
I raise my hand toward heaven and declare that, as surely as I live forever,
when I sharpen my gleaming sword and take hold of judgment, I'll take vengeance on my enemies and repay those who hate me.
I'll make my arrows drunk with blood. My sword will devour flesh, with the blood of the dead and the captives and with the heads of the enemy leaders.”
Rejoice with his people, you nations! He'll avenge the blood of his servants, repay his enemies, and make atonement for his land and his people.
Moses and Joshua son of Nun came and recited all the words of this song for the people to hear.
When Moses finished saying all these words to Israel,
he told them, “Take to heart every word I'm giving you as a witness today. Tell your children to carefully follow every word of this law.
These words matter. They are your life. By living by them, you'll have long lives in the land you're crossing the Jordan to take as your own.”
That same day the LORD spoke to Moses.
“Go up to Mount Nebo in the Abarim range, in Moab across from Jericho. Look out over Canaan, the land I'm giving the Israelites to possess.
You'll die on the mountain you climb and be gathered to your people, just as your brother Aaron died on Mount Hor and was gathered to his people.
This is because you broke faith with me in front of the Israelites at the waters of Meribah at Kadesh, in the wilderness of Zin. You failed to honor my holiness among the Israelites.
You'll see the land from far away, but you won't enter the land I'm giving to the Israelites.”
Before he died, Moses, the man of God, gave the Israelites this blessing.
He said, “The LORD came from Sinai and rose over them from Seir. He shone out from Mount Paran. He came from among tens of thousands of holy ones, with a fiery law for his people at his right hand.
Yes, he loves his people. All his holy ones are in your hand. They sit at your feet, each taking in your words.
Moses gave us the law as an inheritance for the assembly of Jacob.
He was king in Jeshurun when the people's leaders gathered and all Israel's tribes came together.
Let Reuben live and escape death. May his people be many.”
For Judah he said, “LORD, hear Judah's voice and bring him back to his people. He has fought for himself with his own hands. Help him against his enemies.”
About Levi he said, “Your Thummim and Urim belong to your faithful one, whom you tested at Massah and challenged at the waters of Meribah.
He said of his father and mother, ‘I haven't seen them.’ He didn't acknowledge his brothers or recognize even his own children, because the Levites followed your word and kept your covenant.
They'll teach Jacob your rulings and Israel your law. They'll burn incense before you and put whole burnt offerings on your altar.
LORD, bless his abilities and accept what his hands do. Strike down those who rise against him and those who hate him. May they never get up again.”
About Benjamin he said, “The LORD's beloved will live safely beside him. The LORD shelters him all day long, and Benjamin rests between his shoulders.”
About Joseph he said, “The LORD has blessed his land with the best gifts from the sky, with dew and with water from the depths below,
with the finest crops the sun ripens and the best that comes with each moon,
with the best of the ancient mountains and the treasures of the everlasting hills,
with the best of the earth and all it holds, and with the favor of the one who lived in the bush. May all this rest on Joseph's head, on the crown of the one set apart from his brothers.

His firstborn bull has majesty, and his horns are like the horns of a wild ox. With them he'll drive the peoples to the ends of the earth. These are Ephraim's tens of thousands and Manasseh's thousands.”
About Zebulun he said, “Celebrate when you go out, Zebulun, and when you're in your tents, Issachar.
They'll call the peoples to the mountain and offer sacrifices there in righteousness. They'll draw on all the sea provides and the treasures hidden in the sand.”
About Gad he said, “Blessed is the one who gives Gad more room. Gad lives like a lioness, tearing arm and scalp.
He chose the first share for himself, since the lawgiver's portion was reserved for him. He came with the leaders of the people and carried out the LORD's justice and his rulings with Israel.”
About Dan he said, “Dan is a lion cub leaping out of Bashan.”
About Naphtali he said, “Naphtali, you have all the favor you could ask for and are full of the LORD's blessing. Take possession of the west and the south.”
About Asher he said, “Asher is blessed with children. May his brothers welcome him, and may he dip his foot in oil.
Your gate bars will be iron and bronze, and your strength will last as long as you live.
Jeshurun, nobody is like God. He rides through the heavens to help you and across the skies in his majesty.
The eternal God is your home, and his everlasting arms are underneath you. He drove the enemy out before you and said, ‘Destroy them!’
Israel lives in safety, and Jacob's spring flows undisturbed in a land of grain and new wine. Even the sky sends down dew.
How blessed you are, Israel! Who's like you, a people rescued by the LORD? He's your shield and your triumphant sword. Your enemies will submit to you, and you'll tread on their high places.”
Moses went up from the plains of Moab to Mount Nebo, to the top of Pisgah across from Jericho. The LORD showed him all of Gilead as far as Dan,
all of Naphtali, the land of Ephraim and Manasseh, and all of Judah as far as the Western Sea,
as well as the south and the plain of the Jericho Valley, from the city of palm trees as far as Zoar.
The LORD told him, “This is the land I swore to Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob that I would give to their descendants. I've let you see it with your own eyes, but you won't cross over into it.”
So Moses, the LORD's servant, died there in Moab, just as the LORD had said.
The LORD buried him in the valley in Moab across from Beth Peor, and to this day nobody knows where his grave is.
Moses was 120 years old when he died. He could still see clearly and hadn't lost his strength.
The Israelites cried for Moses in the plains of Moab for thirty days, until their time of mourning was over.
Joshua son of Nun was full of the spirit of wisdom because Moses had laid his hands on him. The Israelites listened to Joshua and did what the LORD had commanded Moses.
Since then, no prophet has risen in Israel like Moses, whom the LORD knew face to face.
No one has matched the signs and wonders the LORD sent him to do in Egypt against Pharaoh, all his servants, and his whole land,
or the mighty power and awe-inspiring deeds Moses showed in front of all Israel.
